title: Industrial Cardboard Balers � Procurement, Installation, and Trade-In
description: 1. Description of Requirement This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ) for commercial products and services prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and no separate written solicitation will be issued. Solicitation W9124C-26-Q-A030 is for the delivery, installation, and removal of cardboard baler equipment for the Fort Jackson Logistics Readiness Center (LRC). The requirement includes providing two new vertical cardboard balers, performing turnkey installation, and disconnecting, de?anchoring, rigging, and hauling away two existing Vestil balers. All items shall be new, commercial?grade, and compliant with the specifications and salient characteristics identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Vendors may propose brand?name items or any equal product meeting or exceeding the salient characteristics. This acquisition is a 100% Small Business Set?Aside 2. Line Items The line items for this solicitation are those listed in Section B � Supplies or Services & Prices or Costs of W9124C-26-Q-A030: CLIN 0001: Vertical Cardboard Baler, 5HP, 3PH, 208V (Quantity: 2 Each) CLIN 0002: Turnkey installation package (freight, offloading, rigging, anchoring, electrical tie?in, safety testing, training) (Quantity: 1 Job) CLIN 0003: Removal service for two existing Vestil balers (Quantity: 1 Job) All CLINs must be quoted. Partial quotes will not be accepted. 3. Requirement Description & Brand Name or Equal Basis The Government�s minimum requirements are defined in attached PWS. Vendors shall provide equipment meeting all specifications, including: 5 HP motor 208V, 3?phase power 60?inch chamber Hydraulic/automatic bale ejection Bale weight capacity up to 1,000 lbs Wire guides and �bale full� indicator Full turnkey installation Removal and haul?away of existing balers Brand names are used only to communicate minimum quality and performance. Vendors may propose equal products that meet or exceed all salient characteristics. 4. Delivery Information Delivery requirements shall match Section F � Deliveries or Performance: Delivery Date: On or before 07 October 2026 Delivery Location: W6YM USALRCTR FT JACKSON 12600 Jackson Blvd Columbia, SC 29207?6129 Ship To DoDAAC: W90JUK FOB Point: FOB Destination Acceptance: Government acceptance will occur at the delivery location 5. Site Visit Information A pre?quote site visit will be conducted to allow vendors to inspect the installation area, verify access constraints, and assess removal requirements for the existing balers. Attendance is strongly encouraged but not mandatory. Date: Monday, 17 August 2026 Time: 10:00 AM EST Location: Building 1776, Fort Jackson, SC 29207 Meeting Point: Mission and Installation Contracting Command � Fort Jackson, 4340 Century Div Ave, Fort Jackson, SC 29207 POC for Access: Keishawna S. Jenkins Email: keishawna.s.jenkins.civ@army.mil Phone: 520?671?8048 Vendors must arrive 15-30 minutes early to allow time for visitor processing. All attendees must present a valid government?issued photo ID to gain installation access. Questions arising during the site visit must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist after the visit. No verbal direction or clarification provided during the site visit will change the solicitation requirements. 6. Applicable Solicitation Provisions & Clauses All applicable RFO FAR and RFO DFARS clauses are incorporated by reference in Section I of the attached SF 1449. Full text versions may be accessed electronically at: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide 7. Submission Instructions Quotes shall be submitted in accordance with Section L � Instructions to Offerors: Quote Due Date: 26 August 2026 Time: 10:00 AM EST Submission Method: Email only Submit To: Contract Specialist: Keishawna S. Jenkins � keishawna.s.jenkins.civ@army.mil Contracting Officer (cc): Tequlia D. Holmes � tequlia.d.holmes.civ@army.mil Required submission components: Technical submission demonstrating compliance with the PWS Priced quote for CLINs 0001�0003 Representations & Certifications Past performance references Documentation for any equal items Confirmation of delivery schedule 8. Additional Information SAM Registration: Offerors must be actively registered in SAM.gov. No Partial Awards: Award will be made on an all?or?nothing basis. Evaluation Method: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) per Section M. Questions Deadline: 19 August 2026, 11:00 AM EST.

description: The Virginia Air National Guard is issuing a solicitation for an Invitation for Bids (IFB) to award a single firm-fixed-price contract to Replace the HVAC System at Bldg 203 Redhorse Facility in accordance with specs dated 17 April 2026 and drawings dated 17 April 2026. Work is located at 203d Redhorse Squadron located in Virginia Beach, VA. The contract duration is 180 days after notice to proceed. This project is 100% Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business set aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220, with a size standard of $45,000,000.00. The magnitude of construction is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The solicitation will result in a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. A Site Visit wil be conducted on 6 August 2026 at 1000. title: Amendment for solicitation W911SD26QA117 - Cooking Exhaust Maintenance Services
description: Amendment for solicitation W911SD26QA117: * A Second SITE VISIT for this requirement is scheduled for 21 August 2026 at 11:30 AM EST. * Interested parties will assemble in the front foyer of the Mission Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Bldg.681 Rogers Place, West Point, NY. * A VISITOR PASS IS REQUIRED for entry. Guidance for obtaining a visitor pass from the Visitors Center outside of the Thayer Gate is outlined in PWS Section 1.5. * Visitor Center Address: 2107 New South Post Rd, Highland Falls, NY 10928. * Updated PWS, Building Names & numbers, CLINs, and RFIs will be uploaded in SAM.gov (ID W911SD26QA117) * The solicitation amendment reflecting the updated CLINs will be uploaded once finalized. A separate Excel spreadsheet containing the updated CLINs has been uploaded for reference. * Interested parties are advised to monitor SAM.gov regularly for any updates. General Scope The Directorate of Public Works has requested the contractor to perform services to include, but not limited to the following: 1. Cover all stationary equipment, under and adjacent to exhaust systems being cleaned. 2. Inspect and clean all ducts, louvers, fans, exhaust hoods, exhaust fans, filters and building surfaces where system(s) vent to the outside. 3. Disassemble, inspect, clean, and reassemble all components associated with cooking related exhaust systems. 4. Remove coverings, clean and wipe equipment, and wash floors to remove any grease or associated cleaning debris at USMA. SpaceSavers
description: *THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT* Modular Space-Saving Storage System (SpaceSaver) 1.0 INTRODUCTION This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). This SSS is issued solely for information and planning purposes to conduct market research. It does not constitute a solicitation or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents to this SSS. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the interested party's expense. 2.0 BACKGROUND & SCOPE The Government requires a modular, space-saving, high-density storage system capable of safely storing small boats, U-TC dive equipment, and auxiliary equipment. The system must provide vertical storage capabilities and include ventilated lockers to ensure proper equipment maintenance and lifespan. 3.0 MINIMUM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS The Government is seeking contractors capable of providing a storage system that meets or exceeds the following minimum salient characteristics: 3.1 Team Gear Cabinets (Quantity: 5) Dimensions: Minimum 32� L x 50� W x 96� H Shelf Configuration: 5 shelves total (Bottom three: 32� L x 50� W x 25� H; Top two: 32� L x 50� W x 10� H) Weight Capacity: Must support up to 1,000 lbs distributed weight Ventilation: Must be ventilated to prevent moisture buildup 3.2 Auxiliary Equipment Cabinets (Quantity: 6) Dimensions: Minimum 32� L x 50� W x 96� H Shelf Configuration: 4 equally spaced shelves (32� L x 50� W x 24� H) Weight Capacity: Must support up to 1,000 lbs distributed weight Ventilation: Must be ventilated to prevent moisture buildup 3.3 Boat Storage Capacity: Must safely accommodate vertical/high-density storage of up to 15 small boats (Rolled Wing Boats: L8� / W4� / H4�, approx. dry weight 200 lbs). Requested Footprint: L25� / D8� / H12� Shelf Configuration: Three shelves, 25� in length (1st shelf at base, 2nd shelf at 4�, 3rd shelf at 8�). 3.4 Delivery and Installation Delivery: Delivery of all materials to Moody AFB. Installation: Full on-site installation and assembly services, resulting in a fully operational system. Waste Removal: Removal and disposal of all packaging and trash related to the installation. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties that possess the capabilities to meet this requirement are requested to submit a Capabilities Statement. The statement should be no longer than 3 pages and must include the following: Company Profile: Company Name, Point of Contact, Address, Telephone Number, Email Address, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Socio-Economic Status: Business size standard and any socio-economic categories (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) under the applicable NAICS code. Technical Capability: A brief description of your company's ability to provide the requested storage systems, including product literature, brochures, or past performance examples of similar systems. Available Contracting Vehicles: Indicate if the items are available on GSA Schedule, SEWP, or any other Government-wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC).

title: LMS Cable Gun Lock Procurement
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT IS TO RAISE AWARENESS FOR POTENTIAL OFFERORS. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR OFFERS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTES AND DOES NOT BIND THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD ANY CONTRACT. The Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Suicide Prevention, intends to procure cable-style gun locks with Veterans Crisis Line (VCL) branding in support of lethal means safety and secure firearm storage. The estimated total quantity is 2,100,000 units, delivered in truckload installments over a 12-month period of performance to the VA Hines Health Care Depot, Hines, IL. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is 332510 � Hardware Manufacturing with the size standard of 750 employees. Each unit consists of a 15" heavy-duty steel cable gun lock with a composite body and red vinyl coating (target Pantone 1797), usable on handguns, rifles, and shotguns, and capable of preventing chambering, magazine loading, action engagement, and cylinder movement. Each lock includes two keys, a white VCL logo and phone-number imprint on both sides, an adhesive vinyl VCL crisis-support label affixed to the cable, a plastic VCL wallet card (3.375" x 2.125"), and use instructions, individually packaged and sealed. Locks must be California DOJ-approved, ASTM-compliant, and listed on both the Massachusetts approved firearm safety/locking devices list and the Maryland Approved Integrated Mechanical Safety Devices list. The Government contemplates award of a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract. This is a commercial products acquisition under FAR Part 12. Anticipated period of performance is September 30, 2026, through September 29, 2027. The Government anticipates an award using lowest-price technically acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures. The Government intends to award to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest-priced offer determined to be technically acceptable and conforming to the solicitation requirements. The anticipated award date is September 30, 2026. Questions concerning this announcement should be directed to the Contracting Officer (CO) Chris Binkley at Christopher.Binkley@va.gov.

title: Reduced Oxygen Breathing Device (ROBD) Equipment Maintenance
description: SOURCES SOUGHT/ NOTICE OF INTENT US Army Special Operations Command Reduced Oxygen Breathing Device (ROBD) Equipment Maintenance H92239-26-Q-E015 THIS IS NOT A NOTICE OF SOLICITATION ISSUANCE, BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify interested sources capable of meeting the requirement. The information sought herein is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), invitation for bid (IFB), or as an obligation or commitment on the part of the Government to acquire any product or service. There shall be no basis for claims against the Government as a result of information submitted in response to the RFI. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or otherwise pay for any information submitted by respondents to this request. This notice is for market research purposes only and is not indicative of a full requirement. Should a requirement arise, the full requirement will be detailed in the solicitation. The purpose of this RFI is to identify authorized, certified, and capable industry sources interested in providing comprehensive, off-site maintenance and repair services for six (6) Government-owned ROBD2 units, consisting of: Four (4) Model 6202 units Two (2) Model 6202-1 units To ensure operational safety, device reliability, and compliance with high-altitude simulation standards, responding vendors must possess advanced technical training and verified qualifications specific to these proprietary systems. Only service providers possessing ISO 9001 certification and technicians explicitly trained by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Environics Inc., are qualified for this requirement. Current market research indicates that there is only one vendor capable of fulfilling this specialized requirement. However, it is the Government's intent to evaluate all responses to this Sources Sought notice when making its final determination to negotiate on a sole-source basis. INTERESTED SOURCES CAPABLE OF FULFILLING THIS REQUIREMENT shall submit documentation addressing all required elements listed herein; providing only a reference to a website is unacceptable for purposes of this announcement and will not be considered or reviewed. All proprietary or corporate data received shall be clearly identified and shall be protected from release to sources outside the Government. Contractors interested in providing this service should be registered in the System for Award Management (www.sam.gov). Contractors responding to this Sources Sought are asked to provide the following information: Company's full name, address and Point of Contact information (POC). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Applicable North American Industry Classification Standards (NAICS) codes. Business size (whether they are a large, small, small- disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business etc.). Respondents should advise the Government of pending changes in the business size status. A brief Capability (no more than two pages); which responds to the following questions and demonstrates the ability to meet the requirements specified: Is your company ISO 9001 certified, and do your technicians possess verified Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) training certificates directly from Environics Inc. for ROBD2 equipment (Model 6202 and Model 6202-1)? Please provide brief proof of these credentials. Can your company provide proof of historical work on ROBD equipment maintenance services within the last two (2) years? Does your company possess an adequate facility equipped to manage and perform all diagnostics, calibrations, and physical repairs on ROBD2 hardware, as well as the capacity to provide dedicated remote technical support during standard Government hours (0900 to 1700 EST, Monday through Friday)? Is your company currently compliant with Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 (Self-assessment), or do you have a defined path to verify compliance prior to contract award? FINAL DETERMINATION: Provided no other interested sources with the capability to fulfill this requirement are identified, USASOC intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with ENVIRONICS INC., located at 69 Industrial Park RD E. Tolland, Connecticut, 06084-2873, United States. responses shall be submitted electronically via email to chu.y.ku.civ@socom.mil All responses shall be submitted by 10:00 AM EST on Wednesday, 26 August 2026. Respondents are cautioned that due to file size limitations and e-mail security protocols, there is a risk that not all correspondence will be received by this office. It is the interested parties' responsibility to ensure receipt of all e-mail and faxed correspondence. If receipt has not been acknowledged within 24 hours, please contact the Contracting Office at 910-432-8697. Respondents will NOT be individually notified of the results. However, if the final determination results in the verification of a sole source negotiation, a Notice of Intent to Sole Source and the redacted Justification and Approval will be posted to SAM.gov.

title: USACE SPK Chay Walk-In Freezer Repairs, Monterey CA.
description: 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Sacramento District, intends to specify brand-name-only components manufactured by Kolpak as part of an upcoming firm-fixed-price construction solicitation. Please note that the Government will not purchase these items directly. Instead, the resulting solicitation will require the successful construction prime contractor to procure and install the brand-name components specified below. This notice is published in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(d), �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirement -Brand Name Items.� 2. SPECIFIED BRAND NAME ITEMS The construction contractor will be required to supply and install the following proprietary brand-name Kolpak components to integrate with the existing cold storage unit: Kolpak Drop-in Floor Panels: Custom-fabricated floor panels to fit the exact dimensions of the existing walk-in freezer (approximately 16.5 ft. x 20.5 ft. with an integrated interior door ramp leading to the exterior door) and the adjacent cooler (approximately 16.5 ft. x 11.8 ft.). Kolpak Door Sweep Gasket & Magnetic Door Gaskets (proprietary profiles). Kolpak Heater Wire: 2.5 Watt/FT frame heater wire (thermostatically regulated). Kolpak Door Bumpers: 2-inch low-profile safety bumpers. Kolpak Dial Digital-Thermometer: 2-inch face temperature indicator. Kolpak Exterior Kickplate: 36-inch high, 16-gauge stainless steel protective plate. Kolpak Exterior Door Plug and Frame: Custom stainless steel offset construction. Kolpak Door Threshold: Heavy-duty, 10-gauge stainless steel construction. Kolpak Air Shield: High-velocity air curtain (engineered specifically for Door 123A). Kolpak Interior Floor Ramp: Sloped panel designed to lock into the drop-in floor system. Kolpak Closure Panel & Door Jamb: 22-gauge, 304 stainless steel with built-in heater strip channels. Kolpak Trim Flat: 6 in. x 96 in., 22-gauge stainless steel wall-panel closure trim. 3. JUSTIFICATION FOR BRAND NAME ONLY The existing walk-in freezer and cooler structures at the Chay Dining Facility are proprietary Kolpak assemblies. Alternative modular components utilize incompatible interlocking joints, locking-latch spacing, and panel profiles. The use of brand-name Kolpak components is technically required to: Ensure a hermetic, moisture-tight seal at all structural panel intersections. Prevent thermal bridging, localized cooling loss, condensation, and mold growth. Preserve the mechanical and thermal warranties of the existing modular structures. Fit the pre-existing 36 in. x 84 in. Kolpak doors which are scheduled to be salvaged and reused during the renovation. 4. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS This is not a request for competitive prime construction proposals, and no separate solicitation is available for these brand-name items. However, in accordance with RFO 6.103-1(d), the Government invites potential vendors who manufacture alternative products capable of locking directly into the existing Kolpak modular cam-lock panel profile without field modification, or who are authorized distributors of the specified Kolpak components, to submit a capability statement. Responses must be submitted via email to Antonina Beal at Antonina.Beal@usace.army.mil no later than 26 August 2026 at 10:00 AM Pacific Time. The email subject line must contain the Special Notice number: W9123826X1CBZ. Submissions must include: 1. Company name, address, SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI), CAGE code, and country of product manufacture. 2. Fully detailed technical specification sheets for the proposed alternative items. 3. A detailed technical narrative addressing how your proposed alternative product meets all salient integration features listed above without requiring the complete replacement of the existing structural cold storage unit. A determination by the Government not to compete this brand-name requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: AI TECHNOLOGIES FOR PROCUREMENT MODERNIZATION COMMERCIAL SOLUTIONS OPENING (CSO)
description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Procurement Operations on behalf of the Office of the Chief Procurement Officer (OCPO) Procurement Innovation Lab (PIL) is issuing the subject General Solicitation for DHS and all its Components to rapidly procure commercially available, AI Technologies and solutions for Procurement Modernization to improve the federal procurement process. This capability will be procured using the Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) authority to enable rapid acquisition of innovative, field-ready AI technologies and solutions that address evolving procurement modernization. The CSO is a merit-based solution selection strategy for DHS to acquire innovative commercial items through the use of general solicitation competitive procedures and the award of a contract. "Innovative", within the meaning of this statute, is any new technology, process, or method, including research and development, or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method. "Commercial item" has the same meaning as commercial item under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 2.101, which includes certain commercial services. The CSO General Solicitation aims to identify new ideas, approaches, tools, and partnerships that can help the Department address critical challenges and accelerate transformation across its AI procurement enterprise. This General Solicitation provides a flexible mechanism to solicit, evaluate, and fund exploratory and applied work that does not fit neatly into traditional acquisition frameworks, but that has the potential to improve DHS�s ability to acquire, oversee, and operate within procurement. This procurement is limited to innovative commercial products relevant to the Focus Area outlined in the solicitation. Within the meaning of the statute, innovative is defined as, �Any new technology, process, or method, including research and development, or any new application of an existing technology, process, or method.� Proposals will be evaluated on their individual merits rather than on a comparative basis. Besides the criterion described in the solicitation, the concept paper responses must clearly demonstrate how the commercial item is offered in an innovative manner. The concept papers will be evaluated against the evaluation criteria. Each concept paper submitted may be evaluated against the evaluation criteria separately and need not be evaluated against other concept paper responses submitted by other Offerors. More than one concept paper may be accepted. The Government reserves the right to request interview-style oral presentations or additional written information, if applicable, from one or more Offerors. The Department anticipates that different technologies may address different focus areas and that a portfolio of complementary capabilities may be required to advance the Department�s OT strategy. Industry is invited to respond to this initial General Solicitation addressing the first Focus Area Topic � AI technology. This CSO General Solicitation will stay open for a period of 12 months. The Department intends to use this CSOP to identify, evaluate, and deploy commercial technologies that advance one or more of the Department�s AI Technologies and solutions. Potential Submitters are hereby advised of the following: 1. It is within the Government�s discretion to accept more than one solution for a contract award resulting from this CSO Solicitation. 2. All costs of preparing and submitting solution videos, written submission, and additional presentations/demonstrations related to this CSO Solicitation are the responsibility of the submitting entity and not eligible for funding or reimbursement by the Government. 3. The evaluation will include an assessment of whether the proposed commercial product or service is innovative within the meaning of the statute. Submission and proposals are evaluated on individual merit rather than on a comparative basis, and the Government has considerable latitude in determining which of the submitted proposals it will fund. 4. To be eligible for award, Companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) prior to DHS making a CSO contract award. The first Focus Area Topic under this CSO is AI technology. The government is currently accepting proposals from Offerors that can meet the AI technologies and solutions outlined in the attached General Solicitation. Submissions must be received prior to Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. eastern time. Responses shall be submitted electronically to the following: Mariah.Watt@hq.dhs.gov and Tracy.Miller@hq.dhs.gov. The subject line of the e-mail must be titled �70RDA126R00000009 � AI Technologies for Procurement Modernization.� Note: The Government will review responses as they are submitted and may award at any time. All questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing (via email) to Mariah.Watt@hq.dhs.gov and Tracy.Miller@hq.dhs.gov by Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. eastern time.

title: Roof Replacements – BC18 and BC24 – Beaver Creek Institution - Minimum
description: The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires a qualified contractor to complete the Roof Replacement for buildings BC18 (Unit 2) and BC24 (Unit 3) at Beaver Creek Institution. Objectives: CSC requires a qualified contractor to replace the existing aged asphalt shingle roof with a durable standing seam roofing system that enhances the structural integrity, improves weather resistance and reduces long term maintenance costs. Deliverables: a)The Contractor must ensure that all employees performing work at elevated heights have a valid Working from Heights certification. b)The Contractor must provide all required equipment, including their own equipment for working at heights to complete the work in the project. c)Measurement & Verification 1.Verify all roof dimensions and conditions prior to ordering materials and commencing work. d)Preparation 1.Inspect the roof deck and structure for damage, rot and deficiencies. Report any necessary repairs and provide a quote for additional work. 2. Remove existing vents. 3.Ensure the roof deck is clean and suitable for installation. e) Installation 1.Supply and install a full-coverage synthetic roof underlayment beneath the metal roofing system across all roof areas i. Underlayment must be premium grade, non-perforated synthetic material suitable for use under metal roofing systems ii. Minimum material weight of approximately 200 g/m² (or equivalent) iii. Underlayment must provide a continuous secondary water-shedding barrier over the entire roof deck iv. Material must meet or exceed industry standards for water resistance, tear strength, UV stability, and slip resistance v. Installation must be completed in strict accordance with manufacturer’s specifications vi. Contractor must provide a minimum two (2) year transferable labour warranty covering installation of the underlayment system 2. Install ¾” strapping at manufacturer recommended spacing and orientation for the standing seam system. 3.Install 2” drip edge around the entire perimeter. 4. Supply and install the new snap-lock standing seam roof system, including all accessory components: i. Panels: 24” wide, minimum 24-gauge (0.7mm) gauge thickness. ii. Finish: Hot-dipped zinc coated steel with factory applied colour finish. iii. Attachment: Hidden clip system; all fasteners and components must be corrosion resistant. 5. Supply and install new roof vents, flashing and transitions to match the new roof colour. 6. Provide colour samples to the Site Authority for approval prior to fabrication. 7. Install appropriate sealants for a weather tight finish. 8. Supply and install snow guards at all roof edge areas to prevent snow and ice overhangs and uncontrolled shedding i. Installation must include continuous coverage along the full perimeter of all roof sections, not limited to doors or designated walkways ii. Snow guard layout and spacing must be designed to provide effective snow retention across all roof edges iii. System must be compatible with the installed metal roofing system and designed to avoid damage to roof panels or fasteners iv. Installation must be completed in accordance with accepted industry best practices for metal roofing systems and to maintain roof system integrity and performance f) Compliance & Quality 1. All materials and installation must comply with the manufacturer’s specifications. 2. Provide written warranties for materials, finish, workmanship and service life. g) Site Management 1. Protect surrounding property during work. 2. Maintain a clean worksite and secure materials to prevent wind damage. 3. Dispose of removed roofing material in accordance with environmental and local regulations. 4. The building will be occupied during installation, so the entrance must be protected against falling material. The emergency exits must remain usable throughout the project.

title: Camera-based Fizeau Interferometer
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Dimensional Metrology Group (DMG), located in Gaithersburg, MD, delivers world class dimensional calibration services to support United States manufacturing and other industries. Of particular importance is the calibration of spheres, which serve as reference objects to universal length measuring machines and coordinate measurement machines used internally at NIST and by customers. The NIST DMG is seeking a camera-based Fizeau interferometer to replace ageing equipment responsible for the calibration of the diameter of spheres. A description of the existing equipment and its operation can be found here: https://www.nist.gov/publications/sphere-diameter-interferometry-nanometer-uncertainty.

description: Date of update: 20 August 2026: Combined Synopsis Update 2: The combined synopsis has been extended until Wednesday, 26 August 2026. Date of update: 11 August 2026: Combined Synopsis Update: A.09.01.11 Solicitation Attachment 3 Site Visit Directions Date of posting 6 August 2026: The Performance Work Statement (PWS) defines the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide Preventive (PM), Unscheduled (UM), and Emergency Maintenance (EM) for the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) Vogelweh Headquarters in Germany. The contractor is responsible for providing all qualified labor, management, materials, and specialized tools to ensure the continuous, safe, and compliant operation of all facilities, infrastructure, utilities, and refrigeration systems. Maintenance & Response Protocols: PM: Requires a 100% initial equipment/refrigerant inventory (updated semi-annually) and execution of scheduled checks. UM: Detailed cost estimates must be submitted via the online Service Order Management System (SOMS) within 14 days, with repairs completed within 45 days of approval. EM: Operates 24/7/365 with a 3-hour on-site response time. Repairs under �3,000 must be mitigated or fixed immediately; those exceeding �3,000 require immediate COR coordination. Systems & Data Integrity: All work orders, inventories, and billing must be managed via SOMS. Documentation must be fully compatible with Microsoft Office, and all communication, logs, and briefings must be in English. Environmental & Liability Standards: The contractor is strictly liable for refrigerant management, requiring detailed tracking for units with greater than or equal to 3kg of gas and an annual leak report due every January 30th. Quality & Warranties: Fully incorporates EU Directive 2019/771, providing a 2-year legal guarantee on all parts and installations. Non-conforming work must be corrected within 7 days, or the work order faces cancellation without payment.

It must be capable of safely transporting at least eight 216m rail sections per load, operating on both road and rail, negotiating 5,000m radius curves, maximum 160mm canted sections can't deficiency, 3.50% maximum gradients, and achieving speeds above 10km/h, subject to supplier technical evidence. Suppliers should be able to demonstrate relevant capability and experience in road-rail plant, specialist rail handling equipment, design/modification, certification, testing, operation, and maintenance. FBRS JV is also interested in solutions that support reuse, asset repurposing, and lower-carbon outcomes.

description: The contractor shall provide all labor, management, analysis, planning programming, administration, training, review, transportation and incidentals necessary for one-engine inoperative departure data in order to maximize aircraft operational weights while providing safe escape routings for specified Mission Design Series (MDS) aircraft in accordance with (IAW) this Performance Work Statement (PWS). SDP data shall be delivered to the Government via internet access, email or other avenues for direct-to-aircraft data delivery, for retrieval of data for a specified list of airports, runways, aircraft and engine type and takeoff flap settings in order to enhance the Air Force�s ability to safely and effectively conduct operations from these fields. The contractor shall design and provide a web-based SDP takeoff performance system for the defined Mission Design Series (MDS) based on each aircraft manufacturer�s performance algorithm, as well as real time derived data to make takeoff calculations. Aircraft requiring SDP subscriptions include C-5M, KC-46, C-17, KC-135, C-130J, C-37A, C-21A, and E-3. The government may add new or delete MDS aircraft, as necessary, to the contract list. title: NSWC-PHD MATAC OTA Request for Solutions: Rapid Acquisition & Private-capital Transition for Operational Readiness (RAPTOR)
description: Request for Solutions: Rapid Acquisition & Private-capital Transition for Operational Readiness (RAPTOR) Background and Summary: The Department of the Navy Rapid Capabilities Office (DON RCO) is the single accountable organization spanning all naval warfare domains, tasked with rapidly delivering transformative solutions to the hardest DON operational problems. To execute this mission, the Navy needs a rapid, risk-reduced method to identify, evaluate, and acquire cutting-edge technologies from non-traditional vendors and private capital markets to resolve urgent operational warfighter capability gaps within a one-to-three-year delivery horizon. Purpose: To prototype and validate a new business process framework�delivered as integrated mission advisory and operating-partner services�featuring three distinct workstreams: (1) DONRCO 1.0 Portfolio Performance, encompassing capability shaping, performer diligence, Measure of Effectiveness (MOE) and Measure of Performance (MOP) design, and return on investment (ROI) assessment; (2) DONRCO 2.0 Mission Planning, encompassing platform architecture, standard operating procedures, and a capital coordination and stakeholder engagement framework; and (3) Navy Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) Strategic Deal Support, encompassing strategic deal architecture, contract structuring, and partner/vendor sourcing. This effort directly supports the SECWAR and SECNAV mandate for immediate acquisition reform and the Budget Execution-Year Technology Selection (BETS) portfolio model. Please go to matac.org for additional details

description: SYNOPSIS This is a combined synopsis and solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) FAR Part 12.202(b)(1), as applicable, and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested and a separately written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation documents and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) Number: 2026-01, Effective Date: 03/13/2026 and through the current RFO FAR. The complete text of any of the clauses and provisions are available electronically from the following site: www.acquisition.gov. INSTRUCTIONS AND INFORMATION TO OFFERORS RFO FAR 52.212-1 Instruction to Offerors Commercial Products and Commercial Services This clause applies in its entirety and there are currently no addenda to the provision. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENTS The Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) is seeking Contractors for the procurement of BRAND NAME or EQUAL Space Guard Beast Wire Mesh Guarding System Security Cages to secure high-value laboratory equipment and components in accordance with the requirements and specifications detailed in the attached Purchase Description. This procurement is being conducted using the Simplified Acquisition Procedures authorized in RFO FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The synopsis/solicitation number is W91ZLK-26-Q-A018. This solicitation is issued as as a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under the associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 332618 (Other Fabricated Wire Product Manufacturing), with a small business size standard of 500 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5670. The Government intends to award of a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to the Lowest Priced Technically Acceptable (LPTA) offeror. Technical Acceptability will be based on a quote that meets all the requirements and specifications listed in the attached Purchase Description (PD) Attachment-1. EVALUATION AND BASIS FOR AWARD FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation - Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. Basis for Award: The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Lowest Price, Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures described in RFO FAR 15.103-2 will be used, meaning the award will be made on the basis of the lowest evaluated price of proposals meeting the acceptability standards for the specification requirements. The technical evaluation will be a determination based on information furnished by the Contractor. In order to be considered technically acceptable, Contractor responses must meet all requirements and technical specifications in the Purchase Description (Attachment 1). By submitting a quote, the Contractor agrees to the notations identified in the Purchase Description. To receive consideration for award, a rating of "Acceptable" must be achieved. Acceptability of proposals will be based on meeting all of the requirements and specifications of the Purchase Description. Failure to address each requirement will result in the quote proposal being rated unacceptable. The Government is not responsible for locating or securing any information which is not identified in the offer. The Government reserves the right to make an award without discussions. Partial quotes will not be evaluated by the Government. DETERMINATION OF RESPONSIBILITY 52.212-3, Offeror Representation and Certifications - Commercial Products and Commercial Services. All quotations from responsible and qualified sources will be fully considered. Vendors who are not registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award will not be considered. Vendors may register with SAM online by visiting www.sam.gov. Offerors shall include a completed copy of the provision at FAR 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications- Commercial Products and Commercial Services, with their offer. In accordance with FAR 9.103, contracts will be placed only with Contractors that the Contracting Officer determines to be responsible. Corporate Details: Company name, physical address, website address, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Point of Contact (POC): Name, phone number, and email address. Indicate whether, in your opinion, the product(s) meet the definition of (a) commercial product or (b) commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item or COTS item as described at https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-2 and, if so, which definition applies ((a) or (b)). title: Solicitation- WT 18058173 Airfield and Weather Flight Carpet Replacement
description: This project entails the removal and replacement of flooring approximately 4,370 square foot of carpet on the first floor of Building 122, Peterson Space Force Base (PSFB). The contractor will coordinate with the 21st Civil Engineering Squadron (21 CES) to conduct bio-environmental screening for hazardous materials beneath the existing flooring. Once cleared, the contractor will remove the old carpet and rubber cove base, managing daily site clean-up and off-base debris disposal, as on-site equipment storage is strictly prohibited. To prepare the space, the contractor will relocate standard furniture --coordinating with the Government to ensure all IT cables, power cords, and personal items are removed beforehand. The installation phase requires laying new, commercial-grade modular carpet tiles or planks directly over the existing vinyl flooring using low-VOC adhesives. The contractor will also install a new vinyl cove base, trim door bottoms for proper clearance, and perform any necessary wall spackling and painting to repair damage caused during the removal of the old baseboards. The project will conclude with the repositioning of all furniture and a final Quality Assurance acceptance inspection conducted by 21 CES Operations Flight personnel. Please see attached Combo Solicitation and attachments for detailed information required.

title: 6515--NX EQ Image Guided Surgical Navigation System
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), formerly the Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify qualified sources with the capability and the resources to meet the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program requirement for Image-Guided Surgical Navigation Systems. The EPO in conjunction with VHA is seeking a qualified source to supply brand name or equal Medtronic Stealthstation Image-Guided Surgical Navigation System on an agency-wide basis. VA intends to award a single Requirements Contract with Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) orders IAW FAR 16.503, Requirements Contracts, to a supplier of this equipment. Vendors will be required to deliver complete image-guided stereotactic systems to VA medical centers and facilities throughout the United States. The anticipated period of performance is for one 12-month base period with four 12-month option periods from the date of award. However, the Government's decision as to whether to continue with the contract, upon annual review, will be based upon successful performance during each previous year and continued need. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus and the associated size standard is 1,250 employees. The FAR Provision found at 52.204-7 requires that The Offeror shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation. You may access the SAM website at SAM.gov | Home. All offerors must be certified with the appropriate NAICS code on the SAM website. All SDVOSB/VOSB offerors must be verified in the SBA database at: https://www.sba.gov/veterans/#vetcert at the time of submission. Submissions for this sources sought shall be submitted by email no later than August 26, 2026, 12:00pm Eastern to all the following: Alanna.Wilson@va.gov Sara.Vickroy@va.gov This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this notice. This Sources Sought Notice is part of a continuous process for obtaining the latest information on the commercial status of the industry with respect to their current and near-term abilities. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive contract. It is emphasized that this is a notice solely for planning and informational purposes. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Image-Guided Surgical Navigation System is a stereotactic computer-aided surgical system designed to aid in the performance of minimally invasive procedures by combining medical imaging, dedicated computer software, and instrument tracking systems for guidance. The systems provide real-time, three-dimensional (3D) positioning and orientation of instruments relative to the patient s anatomy on a video display during surgery without requiring the use of an endoscope. Image-guided surgical navigation systems work in a similar way to global positions systems (GPS) applied to the human body. They provide medical images that show the location of the instruments in real time during the procedure, and one or more imaging modalities, such as computed tomography (CT) and/or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), may be used in the procedure. Dedicated image-guided stereotactic systems intended for particular procedures such as neurosurgery, cardiac mapping and ablation, mammographic biopsy, and cranial, spinal, orthopedic, and laryngological surgery procedures are available. Image-guided systems intended to facilitate radio surgical procedures from the exterior of the body are also available. Brief Description of Requirement USARCENT G2 has an enduring operational requirement to provide an expeditionary Top Secret (TS) communications capability in support of the USARCENT Commanding General (CG). The technical TS communications capability is currently provided by the 513th Military Intelligence Brigade (Theater) [513th MIB(T)] Deployable Intelligence Support Element (DISE). To securely employ this capability, a T?SCIF is required. The Government has identified a Radio Frequency (RF) shielded tent with integrated noise?masking equipment as the solution that satisfies the stringent TEMPEST and RF mitigation requirements for TS/SCI operations in austere and expeditionary environments. This solution is required due to its: Compliance with applicable TEMPEST and RF shielding standards for TS/SCI operations Small form factor and ease of transport, setup, and teardown Suitability for repeated deployment in expeditionary and contingency environments Additional technical, performance, and interface requirements are provided in the attached Salient Characteristics, which form an integral part of this notice. 2. Period and Place of Performance Required Delivery Date: No later than 60 calendar days after contract award. Place of Performance / Delivery Location: Shaw Air Force Base, South Carolina (Shaw AFB, SC). Specific delivery instructions, points of contact, and access requirements will be provided at time of award. 3. Anticipated Contract Information Type of Contract: Firm?Fixed Price (FFP) Acquisition Procedures: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services Authority: Sole source procurement under RFO 6.103?1 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 334310 � Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing No formal written solicitation will be issued. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is published in accordance with applicable regulations to notify industry of the Government�s intent to award a sole source contract and to determine if any other sources can meet the Government�s requirements as specified in the attached Salient Characteristics. 4. Responses must include, at a minimum, the following information: a. title: 6515--NX EQ Image Guided Surgical Navigation System
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), formerly the Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify qualified sources with the capability and the resources to meet the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program requirement for Image-Guided Surgical Navigation Systems. The EPO in conjunction with VHA is seeking a qualified source to supply brand name or equal Medtronic Stealthstation Image-Guided Surgical Navigation System on an agency-wide basis. VA intends to award a single Requirements Contract with Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) orders IAW FAR 16.503, Requirements Contracts, to a supplier of this equipment. Vendors will be required to deliver complete image-guided stereotactic systems to VA medical centers and facilities throughout the United States. The anticipated period of performance is for one 12-month base period with four 12-month option periods from the date of award. However, the Government's decision as to whether to continue with the contract, upon annual review, will be based upon successful performance during each previous year and continued need. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus and the associated size standard is 1,250 employees. The FAR Provision found at 52.204-7 requires that The Offeror shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation. You may access the SAM website at SAM.gov | Home. All offerors must be certified with the appropriate NAICS code on the SAM website. All SDVOSB/VOSB offerors must be verified in the SBA database at: https://www.sba.gov/veterans/#vetcert at the time of submission. Submissions for this sources sought shall be submitted by email no later than August 26, 2026, 12:00pm Eastern to all the following: Alanna.Wilson@va.gov Sara.Vickroy@va.gov This notice is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted as a result of this notice. This Sources Sought Notice is part of a continuous process for obtaining the latest information on the commercial status of the industry with respect to their current and near-term abilities. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive contract. It is emphasized that this is a notice solely for planning and informational purposes. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time. 2.0 SCOPE OF WORK The Image-Guided Surgical Navigation System is a stereotactic computer-aided surgical system designed to aid in the performance of minimally invasive procedures by combining medical imaging, dedicated computer software, and instrument tracking systems for guidance. The systems provide real-time, three-dimensional (3D) positioning and orientation of instruments relative to the patient s anatomy on a video display during surgery without requiring the use of an endoscope. Image-guided surgical navigation systems work in a similar way to global positions systems (GPS) applied to the human body. They provide medical images that show the location of the instruments in real time during the procedure, and one or more imaging modalities, such as computed tomography (CT) and/or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), may be used in the procedure. Dedicated image-guided stereotactic systems intended for particular procedures such as neurosurgery, cardiac mapping and ablation, mammographic biopsy, and cranial, spinal, orthopedic, and laryngological surgery procedures are available. Image-guided systems intended to facilitate radio surgical procedures from the exterior of the body are also available. title: Theater Rigging Control System Modernization
description: The Library of Congress (Library) requires contract support to modernize the theatrical rigging control systems for the historic Coolidge Auditorium. The 485-seat venue opened in the 1920�s, designed with acoustic properties to support chamber music. The venue began to support other types of performances, in addition to other types of events. To support increased use, modernization was performed in the mid-1990�s which added motorized theatrical rigging and automation. The legacy infrastructure and system added in the 1990�s was installed by Wenger/JR Clancy, and is characterized by distributed control points, variable motor behavior, and limited system intelligence. The control unit for the system has been inoperable for over a year. The installed infrastructure reflects a rigging ecosystem in which motorized scenic elements were deployed as semi-independent subsystems with limited interoperability and with centralized control unit. At present, these subsystems can only be operated using standalone manual override stations, which are still operable for each component. This modernization effort is intended to unify these systems into a single theater rigging control environment and replace the non-working control unit. All work shall comply with historic preservation constraints, structural limitations, and restricted installation practices typical of protected performance venues. The Contractor shall remove the current theatrical rigging control system and provide a new theatrical rigging control system for the Library�s Coolidge Auditorium. title: Theater Rigging Control System Modernization
description: The Library of Congress (Library) requires contract support to modernize the theatrical rigging control systems for the historic Coolidge Auditorium. The 485-seat venue opened in the 1920�s, designed with acoustic properties to support chamber music. The venue began to support other types of performances, in addition to other types of events. To support increased use, modernization was performed in the mid-1990�s which added motorized theatrical rigging and automation. The legacy infrastructure and system added in the 1990�s was installed by Wenger/JR Clancy, and is characterized by distributed control points, variable motor behavior, and limited system intelligence. The control unit for the system has been inoperable for over a year. The installed infrastructure reflects a rigging ecosystem in which motorized scenic elements were deployed as semi-independent subsystems with limited interoperability and with centralized control unit. At present, these subsystems can only be operated using standalone manual override stations, which are still operable for each component. This modernization effort is intended to unify these systems into a single theater rigging control environment and replace the non-working control unit. All work shall comply with historic preservation constraints, structural limitations, and restricted installation practices typical of protected performance venues. The Contractor shall remove the current theatrical rigging control system and provide a new theatrical rigging control system for the Library�s Coolidge Auditorium.

description: Public Safety Canada is seeking to determine whether there are suppliers qualified under the ProServices Supply Arrangement, Stream 9.15 – Facilitation Consultant, that are capable of meeting the requirements described below. The resulting contract will include the provision of facilitation and support services for three webinars to be delivered during the current fiscal year. Each webinar is expected to be approximately two (2) to two and a half (2.5) hours in duration. The contractor will be required to provide facilitation and event support services, including a virtual platform, registration management, technical support, simultaneous interpretation, and the preparation of reports and/or follow-up documentation. description: The Defense Health Agency (DHA) Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division (HCD) - West, Delta Branch, intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract on a sole-source basis to Parata Systems, LLC, 106 Roche Drive, Durham, NC 27703, utilizing the authority of Title 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented in RFO 6.103-1(c)(1) and RFO 12.102(a) (Commercial Acquisitions - Restriction of Competition under Class Deviation 2026-O0017, Revision 1): For purchases available from only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This requirement is for the BD AutoNotify voice and text messaging subscription service to interface with the existing government-owned proprietary BD IntelliCab Will Call system at the USAF 60th Medical Group Main Pharmacy, located at David Grant USAF Medical Center (DGMC), Travis AFB, CA. BD AutoNotify is an add-on notification service that enables patients to receive automated calls or text messages when their prescription(s) are ready for pickup. The AutoNotify service is not standalone software and does not require local installation on any system; instead, it activates latent features within the existing proprietary software environment. title: CMA and LPN Medical Services � Warm Springs Service Unit
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This requirement is for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order for contracted Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) and Licensed Practical Nurses (LPN) to support the Medical Program at the Warm Springs Service Unit (WSSU), Warm Springs, Oregon. The purpose of this requirement is to provide supplemental professional medical and nursing to ensure continuity of patient care services and access to care. The contracted CMA or LPN shall assist in maintaining safe, accurate, and effective dental services while supporting ongoing clinical operations and compliance with applicable standards of care. Attachment No. 1 � Pricing Schedule, (Supplies or Services and Prices/Costs) Attachment No. 2 � Wage Determination Attachment No. 3 � Business Associate Agreement Attachment No. 4 � IEE Form PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT DENTAL PROVIDER AND DENTAL HYGIENIST SERVICES WARM SPRINGS SERVICE UNIT (WSSU) I. BACKGROUND The Warm Springs Health and Wellness Center�s mission is to provide an innovative, caring, and diverse healthcare system that is trusted and responsive to the needs of the community. The Warm Springs Health and Wellness Center is a primary care clinic that provides quality healthcare to all eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives in the Warm Springs Service Unit Area. The Warm Springs Health and Wellness Center provides a comprehensive system of healthcare services including medical, dental, optometry, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, podiatry, and community health services. The medical program emphasizes prevention, patient education, clinical support, and comprehensive family-oriented dental treatment. Due to limited Purchase/Referred Care (PRC) resources and continued community demand for Nursing services, the Warm Springs Service Unit requires contracted Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) and Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) services to improve access to care and support continuity of patient care. II. OBJECTIVE The objective of this contract is to provide clinical nursing and medical support services for eligible patients of the Warm Springs Service Unit. Services shall include patient assessment, vital signs, clinical support, patient education, care coordination and related medical support services. The contractor shall provide professional CMA and/or LPN services up to five (5) days per week as coordinated with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). III. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE AND LOCATION A. Location Services shall be performed at: Warm Springs Health and Wellness Center 1270 Kot-Num Road Warm Springs, OR 97761 B. Period of Performance The period of performance shall be one year from date of award. C. Clinic Schedule Clinic hours are generally: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 8:00 AM � 5:00 PM Wednesday: 12:00 PM � 5:00 PM The contractor shall be entitled to a one-hour lunch period. The clinic is closed on federally recognized holidays and during emergency or administrative closures. IV. PERFORMANCE-BASED REQUIREMENTS A. Performance Objectives The Contractor shall provide comprehensive performance-based CMA and LPN services that improve access to care, maintain continuity of care, support preventive healthcare initiatives, and ensure high-quality clinical outcomes for eligible beneficiaries of the Warm Springs Service Unit (WSSU). The Contractor shall achieve measurable outcomes consistent with Indian Health Service (IHS) standards, Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) requirements, accepted standards of nursing and clinical practice, and WSSU operational goals. Performance shall be evaluated based on quality of care, patient access, documentation accuracy, professional conduct, clinical productivity, compliance with regulatory requirements, and timely completion of services. B. Performance Standards The Contractor shall: Maintain timely and accurate clinical documentation in RPMS/EHR; Provide nursing care services in accordance with accepted professional standards; Maintain compliance with infection prevention and control standards; Demonstrate professionalism and cultural sensitivity in all patient interactions; Meet scheduled clinic coverage requirements; Coordinate continuity of care and referrals; Comply with HIPAA, Privacy Act, and all applicable federal requirements; Maintain active licensure, certifications, and credentialing throughout the contract period. Performance deficiencies identified by the Government may require corrective action plans and may impact continuation of services. V. Tasks A. General Requirements The contractor shall provide direct patient care services in a responsible, respectful, professional, and caring manner consistent with accepted standards of nursing practice and Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) standards. The contractor shall: Interview and assess patients; Review of medical histories; Perform nursing assessments and evaluations; Record findings and nursing care provided in the electronic health record system (RPMS/EHR); Provide nursing care and respond to urgent/emergency patient needs within the contractors of practice; Coordinate referrals when additional medical or specialty care is required; Provide patient education and health promotion/prevention services; Maintain compliance with HIPAA and all applicable federal regulations; Utilize RPMS/EHR, Microsoft Office, Outlook, and other required systems; Collaborate with medical providers, nursing staff, and community health programs. The contractor shall document all patient care in accordance with WSSU policies and standards. B. CMA Services 1. CMA Task Requirements The CMA Contractor shall independently perform professional medical assisting services within the scope of granted clinical privileges and certification or registration. CMA responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Interviewing and obtaining patient information; Reviewing and evaluating medical histories and current health status; Performing clinical support activities within scope of practice; Obtaining and recording Vital signs withing scope of practice; Assisting providers with examinations, procedures, and patient care; Performing clinical procedures within scope of practice and applicable orders; Providing patient education and health promotion services; Preparing patients for examinations and procedures; Collecting and preparing specimens as authorized and within scope of practice; Coordinating referrals and follow-up care; Providing patient support and follow-up care; Documenting all patient encounters and clinical support services in RPMS/EHR; Collaborating with medical providers, nursing staff, and other clinical and support staff as appropriate; Ensuring continuity of patient care. 2. CMA Performance Outcomes The CMA Contractor shall: Deliver comprehensive medical assisting services consistent with accepted standards of medical assisting practice; Maintain accurate and timely patient records; Demonstrate professional clinical judgment within scope of practice; Maintain productivity and clinic efficiency; Ensure compliance with infection control standards; Provide culturally appropriate patient care; Coordinate continuity of care and referrals effectively. C. LPN Services 1. LPN Task Requirements The LPN Contractor provides preventive, clinical, and therapeutic nursing services within the scope of state licensure and granted privileges. LPN responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Performing patient health assessments and risk assessments as permitted within scope of practice; Reviewing and documenting patient health history; Recording blood pressure and applicable screening information; Performing appropriate health screenings and assessments; Completing nursing assessments an

title: 76--Intent to Award
description: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) has a requirement for a sole source Purchase Order with CPM Group LLC for one year of precious metals advisory services. The period of performance of the resulting award will be 9/16/2026 through 9/15/2027. The U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodities Section of the National Minerals Information Center requests a 1-year subscription for 5 users to a monthly precious metals reports and reports for 5 users to the gold, silver, platinum-group metals, precious metals, copper, niobium, and tantalum supply chain for the North American marketplace. The subscription helps mineral commodity specialists gather valuable information, enhancing their expertise in their role as the principal USGS contact point for the mineral commodities to which they are assigned, and in reporting on important industry developments through monthly, quarterly, and annual USGS publications. Therefore, it intends to make a direct award to CPM Group LLC, on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). This is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals but rather an intent to sole source notification. Questions or concerns may be addressed to the Contract Specialist, Jonathan Wyatt jonathan_wyatt@ios.doi.gov no later than 8/26/2026 The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) considers employee signatures to be Personal Protected Information, and therefore all employee signatures have been redacted. By posting this document, the Contracting Officer attests all appropriate signatures have been obtained. 1. Contracting Agency and Activity The Department of the Interior, United States Geological Survey, Reston Acquisitions Branch, Reston, VA. 2. Nature of Action Being Approved. For award of a non-competitive firm fixed price purchase order for reports from CPM Group. The period of performance is 09/16/2026 to 09/15/2027. 3. Description of Supplies or Services. Required by the Mineral Commodity Specialists in the Mineral Commodities Section and the Minerals Intelligence Research Section of the National Minerals Information Center (NMIC) requires a 1-year subscription for reports on copper, gold, silver, platinum group metals, precious metals, tantalum, niobium, base metals, hafnium, iridium, cesium, and scandium. 4. Statutory Authority The proposed action may be awarded on a sole source basis under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). 5. Rationale Supporting Use of Citation in No. 5. CPM Group provides unique features to meet the Governments minimum needs, such as comprehensive yearbooks on gold, silver, and platinum-group metals as well as outlook reports on cesium, copper, hafnium, iridium, niobium, precious metals, scandium, and tantalum in the United States and globally. CPM Group provides coverage of events and activities that are related to metal mining, extraction, development, production of refined metal, trade, technology, governmental issues and recycling. Notably, the information provided on these critical and precious metals is not found elsewhere. CPM Groups offering contains information on the listed metals that is not available from others doing similar work. Although there are several vendors who provide this type of information, many of them specialize in certain metals but do not have coverage for several of the listed metals, or their offerings do not include vital information. The information enhances mineral commodity specialists� and NMIC economists an understanding of issues and activities in the respective industries and is regularly used in USGS publications. 6. The Efforts to Identify Additional Sources Including the Market Research Conducted. Through working in minerals information regularly and for a long period of time, requestor is familiar with other potential sources. Those sources do not provide the unique combination of breadth and scope of developments in the precious metals industry in the United States and globally that CPM Group reports provide. A pre-solicitation notice was posted without response. In addition to the pre-solicitation notice, the employees who use the reports produced by CPM Group regularly conduct internet searches for potential vendors and are often sent information soliciting business by potential providers. Evaluations of similar products showed that other vendors do not provide coverage of some of the metals for which information is needed. This market research concluded that no other potential vendor could provide the required services. 7. Future Plans to Permit Competition. Future requirements will undergo market research and be competed to the maximum extent practical

description: Description: The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Library Program requires Video Game collection development point system that allow Dept of the Air Force Libraries Division to meet their video game demand. Product characteristics or an equal item must meet to be considered: 1. Must be able to provide materials for collection development in formats that include video games 2. Must be able to provide material of new releases, current best sellers as well as a back catalog of older material 3. Must be able to have 63 libraries individual order accounts under a main account for VCL to manage points 4. Must mail video games up to 63 libraries around the world, shipping costs included in quote 5. Must be able to offer ordering through an online ordering system for 63 libraries 6. Must be able to dedicate customer service representative to resolve all service issues 7. Must be able to provide video games in the following formats: Xbox 1 & X, Playstation 4/5, & Nintendo Switch 8. Must provide a pre-release list to plan upcoming months boxes mut be available on commercial website available for all video game buyers 9. Must provide a suggested monthly order list to DAF libraries. This would be a prefilled cart of newly released suggested titles in DAF Libraries account. 10. Shall provide a commercially available website with an existing multi-tier web-based purchasing system for review and selection of available video games. The system shall offer access to information about publications such as reviews, selection lists, release dates, publisher's list prices, video game covers, descriptions, etc. 11. DAF Libraries does NOT need/want a custom site. We are looking for a video game wholesaler in the library or video game marketplace. 12. DAF 63 Libraries shall have their own unique logins to select items, build carts, and submit selections. 13. Items received in error or in unacceptable condition shall be replaced and shipped to the customer at no additional cost. Return of such items shall not be required. The return window will be more than 30 days due to delays in receiving due to shipping locations. 14. Firm-Fixed Price Order with shipping costs included 15. Shipping shall be via U.S. Postal Service First Class and Priority Mail or similar to APO addresses, either New York, NY or San Francisco, CA. No international shipping is required. 16. No technical or physical processing is required 17. The vendor shall ship items in complete set of 6 games per 20 locations on a monthly basis. Kits must be packaged and labeled separately for each location. 18. Must be able to dedicate a customer service representative to resolve all service issues. 19.
